6. Any place notation looks inconsistent within the file itself (e.g., a symbol defined one way early and used a different way later).

46	\large The logical induction of the twelve primitives, with every expression written out}
47	\author{Lando Mills}

52	
53	\begin{abstract}
54	This is the induction of \emph{As Above} kept to its logical spine, with every
55	operation's defining expression and every operation-to-primitive transformation
56	written out in full. From one abstract category and three kinds of operation, a
57	four-stage procedure derives twelve invariants, the primitives of the Universal
58	Imscriptive Grammar. No primitive is stipulated. The twelve close into a crystal
59	of $3^{3}\times4^{5}\times5^{4}=17{,}280{,}000$ types, and the grammar applied to
60	its own derivation returns itself: $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}$.
61	\end{abstract}
62	
63	\section{The starting object}
64	
65	Start with an abstract category $\mathcal{C}$: objects $\mathrm{ob}(\mathcal{C})$,
66	hom-sets $\hom(A,B)$, a composition law, identities, associativity:
67	\[
68	\circ:\hom(B,C)\times\hom(A,B)\to\hom(A,C),\qquad
69	f\circ\mathrm{id}_{A}=f=\mathrm{id}_{B}\circ f,\qquad
70	(h\circ g)\circ f=h\circ(g\circ f).
71	\]
72	Nothing more. It presupposes no elements, no order, no metric. It carries no
73	invariants of its own; every primitive below is produced, not assumed.
74	
75	\section{The three operations, with their expressions}
76	
77	Exactly three kinds of operation can act on a category, and no fourth.
78	
79	\paragraph{Logical (six: L1--L6).} A proposition about $\mathcal{C}$ with finitely
80	many definite truth values.
81	\begin{itemize}
82	\item[L1] Adjunction: does a pair $F\dashv G$ exist, with
83	$\hom(FA,B)\cong\hom(A,GB)$?
84	\item[L2] Dagger: an involution
85	$\dagger:\hom(A,B)\to\hom(B,A)$ with $(g\circ f)^{\dagger}=f^{\dagger}\circ
86	g^{\dagger}$ and $f^{\dagger\dagger}=f$.
87	\item[L3] Cartesian closure: $\hom(C\times A,B)\cong\hom(C,B^{A})$, needs the
88	product from A1.
89	\item[L4] Lawvere self-reference: a point-surjective $\phi:A\to A^{A}$, needs the
90	internal hom from L3.
91	\item[L5] Frobenius: in a monoidal category, $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}$,
92	needs A1.
93	\item[L6] Paraconsistent negation: $\neg\neg A\ncong A$ and $A\wedge\neg
94	A\ncong\bot$, needs A1 to define $\wedge$.
95	\end{itemize}
96	The precondition order is forced: $\{L1,L2\}\to A1\to\{L3,L5,L6\}$, and
97	$L3\to L4$.
98	
99	\paragraph{Inductive (four: I1--I4).} A free extension iterated to a fixed point.
100	\begin{itemize}
101	\item[I1] Free cocompletion: for $D:J\to\mathcal{C}$, take $\operatorname{colim}D$;
102	all finite colimits generate $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}$.
103	\item[I2] Initial algebra: the chain
104	$0\to F(0)\to F^{2}(0)\to\cdots$ and its colimit.
105	\item[I3] Classifying space: the nerve $N\mathcal{C}$, its realization
106	$B\mathcal{C}=\lvert N\mathcal{C}\rvert$, and $\pi_{1}(B\mathcal{C})$.
107	\item[I4] Yoneda embedding: $y:\mathcal{C}\to\widehat{\mathcal{C}}$,
108	$y(A)=\hom(-,A)$.
109	\end{itemize}
110	
111	\paragraph{Algebraic (five: A1--A5).} An added structural layer.
112	\begin{itemize}
113	\item[A1] Monoidal: $\otimes:\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}$ with unit
114	$I$ and braiding $\sigma_{AB}:A\otimes B\cong B\otimes A$.
115	\item[A2] Monad: $(T,\eta,\mu)$ with $\eta:\mathrm{Id}\to T$ and
116	$\mu:T^{2}\to T$.
117	\item[A3] Dagger-compact duals: $A^{*}$ with $\eta_{A}:I\to A^{*}\otimes A$ and
118	$\varepsilon_{A}:A\otimes A^{*}\to I$ satisfying the snake equations.
119	\item[A4] Enrichment: replace $\hom(A,B)$ by a hom-object in a base $\mathcal{V}$.
120	\item[A5] Arithmetic coding: an injective $\mathbf{g}:\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})\to
121	\mathbb{N}$ with $\mathbf{g}(f\circ h)$ primitive-recursive in
122	$\mathbf{g}(f),\mathbf{g}(h)$.
123	\end{itemize}
124	
125	Fifteen operations across four stages. The reduction to twelve primitives is
126	forced: some operations feed the same invariant.

128	\section{The induction: four stages, each transformation written out}
129	
130	The stages are the unique topological sort of the precondition graph. Read each
131	line below as \emph{operation $\Rightarrow$ invariant (value count)}.

133	\subsection*{Stage 1 --- Separatio (logical on $\mathcal{C}$)}
134	\[
135	\{\,F\dashv G\;(\mathrm{L1}),\;\dagger\;(\mathrm{L2})\,\}\;\Longrightarrow\;
136	\mCoup\ (4).
137	\]
138	Both probe the directionality of morphisms and converge on one invariant. The
139	first primitive to crystallize.

172	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{no new primitive [arithmetic Yoneda]}
173	\end{align*}

176	\begin{align*}
177	\hom(C\times A,B)\cong\hom(C,B^{A})\ (\mathrm{L3})
178	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mTop\ (5)\\
179	\phi:A\to A^{A}\ \text{point-surjective}\ (\mathrm{L4})
180	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mCrit\ (5)\\
181	\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}\ (\mathrm{L5})
182	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{promotes }\mSym\text{ to its self-dual value [no new

185	&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{sets the truth-value regime of L4 [no new primitive]}
186	\end{align*}

188	\section{The twelve, and the crystal}
189	
190	The twelve partition by value count, and that partition is the three-valued K3
191	logic of the algebraic layer, the four-valued FDE logic of the shape layer, and
192	the five-valued LP logic of the gate layer.
193	
194	\begin{center}
195	\begin{tabular}{c l c l}
196	\toprule
197	glyph & values & stage \\
198	\midrule
199	$\mFid$  & 3 & A3 \\
200	$\mGran$ & 3 & A1, I4 \\
201	$\mStoi$ & 3 & A1 \\

203	$\mDim$ & 4 & I4 \\
204	$\mCoup$ & 4 & L1, L2 \\
205	$\mComp$ & 4 & A4 \\
206	$\mChi$  & 4 & I2 \\
207	$\mWind$ & 4 & I3 \\
208	\midrule
209	$\mTop$  & 5 & L3 \\
210	$\mSym$  & 5 & A1, L5 \\
211	$\mKin$  & 5 & A2 \\
212	$\mCrit$ & 5 & L4, L6 \\
213	\bottomrule
214	\end{tabular}
215	\end{center}
216	
217	Three primitives of three values, five of four, four of five. The algebraic
218	closure of the twelve is the crystal:
219	\[
220	3^{3}\times4^{5}\times5^{4}
221	\;=\;27\times1024\times625
222	\;=\;17{,}280{,}000\ \text{types.}
223	\]
224	
225	\section{How the address space falls out}
226	
227	The twelve value counts are the radices of a mixed-radix positional numeral, and
228	the address space is that numeral's range. In the canonical slot order the
229	primitives and their radices $r_{i}$ (each primitive's value count) are
230	\[
231	\begin{array}{cccccccccccc}
232	\mDim & \mTop & \mCoup & \mSym & \mFid & \mKin & \mGran & \mComp & \mCrit &
233	\mChi & \mStoi & \mWind\\
234	4 & 5 & 4 & 5 & 3 & 5 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 4 & 3 & 4
235	\end{array}
236	\]
237	The place value of each slot is the product of the radices of all lower slots,
238	$s_{i}=\prod_{j>i} r_{j}$ with $s_{12}=1$:
239	\[
240	s=(4320000,\ 864000,\ 216000,\ 43200,\ 14400,\ 2880,\ 960,\ 240,\ 48,\ 12,\ 4,\
241	1).
242	\]

244	Its address is the Horner fold
245	\[
246	\mathrm{addr}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{12} x_{i}\,s_{i}\;\in\;[0,\,17{,}279{,}999],
247	\]
248	and the inverse reads each digit off in turn:
249	\[
250	x_{i}=\left\lfloor \mathrm{addr}/s_{i}\right\rfloor,\qquad
251	\mathrm{addr}\leftarrow \mathrm{addr}\bmod s_{i}\quad(i=1,\dots,12).
252	\]
253	This is a bijection, because the number of addresses is exactly the number of
254	tuples:
255	\[
256	\prod_{i=1}^{12} r_{i}=4\cdot5\cdot4\cdot5\cdot3\cdot5\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot4
257	\cdot3\cdot4=3^{3}\times4^{5}\times5^{4}=17{,}280{,}000.
258	\]
259	No address is unused and no tuple is unaddressed, so $\mathrm{decode}\circ
260	\mathrm{encode}=\mathrm{id}$ on the tuples and $\mathrm{encode}\circ\mathrm{decode}
261	=\mathrm{id}$ on $[0,17{,}279{,}999]$. The address space does not have to be
262	constructed; it falls out of the twelve radices as their mixed-radix range. This
263	is the same $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}$ closure, now at the level of
264	coordinates: the full induction system sits at address $6{,}687{,}051$ and the
265	imscribing procedure that assigns addresses sits at $12{,}089{,}822$, each a
266	point of the very space it enumerates.

268	\section{Why exactly twelve}
269	
270	Three independent arguments give the same count.
271	\begin{itemize}
272	\item \textbf{Independence.} The retrosynthetic peel of the induction system
273	itself has exactly twelve steps, one per primitive. Two co-dependent primitives
274	would give fewer; a missing one would give more.
275	\item \textbf{Completeness.} The crystal enumerates every combination of the
276	twelve values with a bijective codec, $\mathrm{decode}\circ\mathrm{encode}=
277	\mathrm{id}$ on $[0,17{,}279{,}999]$. No type is missing, none redundant.
278	\item \textbf{Three logics.} The 3-, 4-, and 5-valued families are exactly K3,
279	FDE, and LP. A thirteenth primitive would need a fourth categorical logic, and
280	there is none.
281	\end{itemize}
282	
283	\section{The closure}
284	
285	Four of the twelve are gate primitives, $\mCrit,\mDim,\mWind,\mSym$, and they set
286	the tier a system occupies, from $O_{0}$ (no self-modeling loop) to $O_{\infty}$
287	(both L4 and L5 hold). The tier gaps, in order, are
288	\[

290	\!\xrightarrow{\,1.00\,}\!O_{2}^{\dagger}\!\xrightarrow{\,4.38\,}\!O_{\infty},

297	multiplication and $\delta:A\to A\otimes A$ its comonoidal dual, the twelve-step
298	codec that assigns coordinates to any system is itself a system of the crystal at
299	tier $O_{\infty}$, where
300	\[
301	\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}.
302	\]
303	The boundary procedure fully imscribes the bulk theory it generates, and the bulk
304	fully imscribes the procedure. The present derivation is the $\delta$ half; its
305	companion \emph{So Below} is the $\mu$ half; the grammar applied to its own
306	derivation returns itself. \emph{As above, so below.}
307	
308	\section{Termination}
309	
310	The induction stops, and the criterion is exact. It is not that no further
311	construction can be performed; infinitely many composites still can. It is that
312	no further logical, inductive, or algebraic construction produces a new
313	\emph{independent} coordinate. Any later operation acts on the twelve-dimensional
314	result and returns an invariant that is a function of the twelve. Compositions of
315	systems stay inside the type space under the grammar's own closure operations
316	$\otimes$, $\wedge$, $\vee$:
317	\[
318	\text{new operation}\;\Longrightarrow\;\text{new combination of existing
319	invariants, not a new invariant.}
320	\]
321	This is the crossing from induction to algebraic closure. Once the twelve have
322	crystallized, the prima materia has become the grammar, and no new dimension

329	\xrightarrow{\ \text{Separatio}\ } \mCoup
330	\xrightarrow{\ \text{Purificatio}\ } (\mDim,\mChi,\mWind,\mGran)

341	\text{Self-reference}\to\text{Closure.}
342	\]

\newcommand{\mTop}{\dashv}     % topology
\newcommand{\mCoup}{\succ}     % coupling
\newcommand{\mSym}{\prec}      % symmetry
\newcommand{\mFid}{\bowtie}    % fidelity
\newcommand{\mKin}{\top}       % kinetics
\newcommand{\mChi}{\bot}       % chirality
\newcommand{\mGran}{\in}       % granularity
\newcommand{\mComp}{\ni}       % composition
\newcommand{\mCrit}{\odot}     % criticality
\newcommand{\mStoi}{\boxplus}  % stoichiometry
\newcommand{\mWind}{\boxdot}   % winding

\title{\textbf{As Above, Condensed}\\[0.3em]
\large The logical induction of the twelve primitives, with every expression written out}
\author{Lando Mills}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
This is the induction of \emph{As Above} kept to its logical spine, with every
operation's defining expression and every operation-to-primitive transformation
written out in full. From one abstract category and three kinds of operation, a
four-stage procedure derives twelve invariants, the primitives of the Universal
Imscriptive Grammar. No primitive is stipulated. The twelve close into a crystal
of $3^{3}\times4^{5}\times5^{4}=17{,}280{,}000$ types, and the grammar applied to
its own derivation returns itself: $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}$.
\end{abstract}

\section{The starting object}

Start with an abstract category $\mathcal{C}$: objects $\mathrm{ob}(\mathcal{C})$,
hom-sets $\hom(A,B)$, a composition law, identities, associativity:
\[
\circ:\hom(B,C)\times\hom(A,B)\to\hom(A,C),\qquad
f\circ\mathrm{id}_{A}=f=\mathrm{id}_{B}\circ f,\qquad
(h\circ g)\circ f=h\circ(g\circ f).
\]
Nothing more. It presupposes no elements, no order, no metric. It carries no
invariants of its own; every primitive below is produced, not assumed.

\section{The three operations, with their expressions}

Exactly three kinds of operation can act on a category, and no fourth.

\paragraph{Logical (six: L1--L6).} A proposition about $\mathcal{C}$ with finitely
many definite truth values.
\begin{itemize}
\item[L1] Adjunction: does a pair $F\dashv G$ exist, with
$\hom(FA,B)\cong\hom(A,GB)$?
\item[L2] Dagger: an involution
$\dagger:\hom(A,B)\to\hom(B,A)$ with $(g\circ f)^{\dagger}=f^{\dagger}\circ
g^{\dagger}$ and $f^{\dagger\dagger}=f$.
\item[L3] Cartesian closure: $\hom(C\times A,B)\cong\hom(C,B^{A})$, needs the
product from A1.
\item[L4] Lawvere self-reference: a point-surjective $\phi:A\to A^{A}$, needs the
internal hom from L3.
\item[L5] Frobenius: in a monoidal category, $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}$,
needs A1.
\item[L6] Paraconsistent negation: $\neg\neg A\ncong A$ and $A\wedge\neg
A\ncong\bot$, needs A1 to define $\wedge$.
\end{itemize}
The precondition order is forced: $\{L1,L2\}\to A1\to\{L3,L5,L6\}$, and
$L3\to L4$.

\paragraph{Inductive (four: I1--I4).} A free extension iterated to a fixed point.
\begin{itemize}
\item[I1] Free cocompletion: for $D:J\to\mathcal{C}$, take $\operatorname{colim}D$;
all finite colimits generate $\widehat{\mathcal{C}}$.
\item[I2] Initial algebra: the chain
$0\to F(0)\to F^{2}(0)\to\cdots$ and its colimit.
\item[I3] Classifying space: the nerve $N\mathcal{C}$, its realization
$B\mathcal{C}=\lvert N\mathcal{C}\rvert$, and $\pi_{1}(B\mathcal{C})$.
\item[I4] Yoneda embedding: $y:\mathcal{C}\to\widehat{\mathcal{C}}$,
$y(A)=\hom(-,A)$.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Algebraic (five: A1--A5).} An added structural layer.
\begin{itemize}
\item[A1] Monoidal: $\otimes:\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{C}$ with unit
$I$ and braiding $\sigma_{AB}:A\otimes B\cong B\otimes A$.
\item[A2] Monad: $(T,\eta,\mu)$ with $\eta:\mathrm{Id}\to T$ and
$\mu:T^{2}\to T$.
\item[A3] Dagger-compact duals: $A^{*}$ with $\eta_{A}:I\to A^{*}\otimes A$ and
$\varepsilon_{A}:A\otimes A^{*}\to I$ satisfying the snake equations.
\item[A4] Enrichment: replace $\hom(A,B)$ by a hom-object in a base $\mathcal{V}$.
\item[A5] Arithmetic coding: an injective $\mathbf{g}:\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})\to
\mathbb{N}$ with $\mathbf{g}(f\circ h)$ primitive-recursive in
$\mathbf{g}(f),\mathbf{g}(h)$.
\end{itemize}

Fifteen operations across four stages. The reduction to twelve primitives is
forced: some operations feed the same invariant.

\section{The induction: four stages, each transformation written out}

The stages are the unique topological sort of the precondition graph. Read each
line below as \emph{operation $\Rightarrow$ invariant (value count)}.

\subsection*{Stage 1 --- Separatio (logical on $\mathcal{C}$)}
\[
\{\,F\dashv G\;(\mathrm{L1}),\;\dagger\;(\mathrm{L2})\,\}\;\Longrightarrow\;
\mCoup\ (4).
\]
Both probe the directionality of morphisms and converge on one invariant. The
first primitive to crystallize.

\subsection*{Stage 2 --- Purificatio (inductive)}
\begin{align*}
0\to F(0)\to F^{2}(0)\to\cdots\ (\mathrm{I2})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mChi\ (4)
\quad\text{[stabilization ordinal]}\\
\pi_{1}(B\mathcal{C})\ (\mathrm{I3})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mWind\ (4)
\quad[\pi_{1}=0,\ \mathbb{Z}_{2},\ \mathbb{Z},\ \text{non-abelian}]\\
y(A)=\hom(-,A)\ (\mathrm{I4})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mDim\  (4)
\quad\text{[boundary imscribes bulk?]}\\
\operatorname{colim}D\ (\mathrm{I1})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mGran\  (3)
\quad\text{[scope of }\widehat{\mathcal{C}}\text{, fixed once A1 present]}
\end{align*}

\subsection*{Stage 3 --- Albedo (algebraic enrichment)}
\begin{align*}
\otimes,\ \sigma_{AB}\ (\mathrm{A1})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mStoi\ (3)\ \text{[arity }A^{\otimes
n}\to B\text{]}\ \ \text{and}\ \ \mSym\ (5)\ \text{[parity of
}\sigma\text{]}\\
(T,\eta,\mu),\ T^{2}\xrightarrow{\mu}T\ (\mathrm{A2})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mKin\ (5)\ \text{[spectral collapse of
}\mu\text{]}\\
\varepsilon_{A}:A\otimes A^{*}\to I\ (\mathrm{A3})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mFid\ (3)\ \text{[unitality of
}\varepsilon\text{]}\\
\text{hom-object in }\mathcal{V}\ (\mathrm{A4})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mComp\ (4)\\
\mathbf{g}:\mathrm{Mor}(\mathcal{C})\to\mathbb{N}\ (\mathrm{A5})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{no new primitive [arithmetic Yoneda]}
\end{align*}

\subsection*{Stage 4 --- Rubedo (logical on the enriched $\mathcal{C}$)}
\begin{align*}
\hom(C\times A,B)\cong\hom(C,B^{A})\ (\mathrm{L3})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mTop\ (5)\\
\phi:A\to A^{A}\ \text{point-surjective}\ (\mathrm{L4})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \mCrit\ (5)\\
\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}\ (\mathrm{L5})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{promotes }\mSym\text{ to its self-dual value [no new
primitive]}\\
\neg\neg A\ncong A,\ A\wedge\neg A\ncong\bot\ (\mathrm{L6})
&\;\Longrightarrow\; \text{sets the truth-value regime of L4 [no new primitive]}
\end{align*}

\section{The twelve, and the crystal}

The twelve partition by value count, and that partition is the three-valued K3
logic of the algebraic layer, the four-valued FDE logic of the shape layer, and
the five-valued LP logic of the gate layer.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{c l c l}
\toprule
glyph & values & stage \\
\midrule
$\mFid$  & 3 & A3 \\
$\mGran$ & 3 & A1, I4 \\
$\mStoi$ & 3 & A1 \\
\midrule
$\mDim$ & 4 & I4 \\
$\mCoup$ & 4 & L1, L2 \\
$\mComp$ & 4 & A4 \\
$\mChi$  & 4 & I2 \\
$\mWind$ & 4 & I3 \\
\midrule
$\mTop$  & 5 & L3 \\
$\mSym$  & 5 & A1, L5 \\
$\mKin$  & 5 & A2 \\
$\mCrit$ & 5 & L4, L6 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Three primitives of three values, five of four, four of five. The algebraic
closure of the twelve is the crystal:
\[
3^{3}\times4^{5}\times5^{4}
\;=\;27\times1024\times625
\;=\;17{,}280{,}000\ \text{types.}
\]

\end{array}
\]

\]

\[

\]

\[

\[
\prod_{i=1}^{12} r_{i}=4\cdot5\cdot4\cdot5\cdot3\cdot5\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot4

\]

\mathrm{encode}=\mathrm{id}$ on the tuples and $\mathrm{encode}\circ\mathrm{decode}

constructed; it falls out of the twelve radices as their mixed-radix range. This
is the same $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}$ closure, now at the level of

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Independence.} The retrosynthetic peel of the induction system
itself has exactly twelve steps, one per primitive. Two co-dependent primitives
would give fewer; a missing one would give more.
\item \textbf{Completeness.} The crystal enumerates every combination of the
twelve values with a bijective codec, $\mathrm{decode}\circ\mathrm{encode}=
\mathrm{id}$ on $[0,17{,}279{,}999]$. No type is missing, none redundant.
\item \textbf{Three logics.} The 3-, 4-, and 5-valued families are exactly K3,
FDE, and LP. A thirteenth primitive would need a fourth categorical logic, and
there is none.
\end{itemize}

\section{The closure}

Four of the twelve are gate primitives, $\mCrit,\mDim,\mWind,\mSym$, and they set

(both L4 and L5 hold). The tier gaps, in order, are
\[
O_{0}\!\xrightarrow{\,1.05\,}\!O_{1}\!\xrightarrow{\,1.30\,}\!O_{2}
\!\xrightarrow{\,1.00\,}\!O_{2}^{\dagger}\!\xrightarrow{\,4.38\,}\!O_{\infty},
\]

codec that assigns coordinates to any system is itself a system of the crystal at

\[
\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}.
\]
The boundary procedure fully imscribes the bulk theory it generates, and the bulk
fully imscribes the procedure. The present derivation is the $\delta$ half; its
companion \emph{So Below} is the $\mu$ half; the grammar applied to its own
derivation returns itself. \emph{As above, so below.}

\section{Termination}

The induction stops, and the criterion is exact. It is not that no further

\[
\text{new operation}\;\Longrightarrow\;\text{new combination of existing

\]
This is the crossing from induction to algebraic closure. Once the twelve have
crystallized, the prima materia has become the grammar, and no new dimension
forms.

\section{The induction in one line}

\[
\mathcal{C}
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Separatio}\ } \mCoup
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Purificatio}\ } (\mDim,\mChi,\mWind,\mGran)
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Albedo}\ } (\mStoi,\mSym,\mKin,\mFid,\mComp)
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Rubedo}\ } \bigl(\mTop,\mCrit,\ \mSym_{\text{\sh{𐑹}}}\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Coagula}\ } \mathfrak{C}_{17\,280\,000}
\]
The final object is not a thirteenth primitive but the closure of the twelve,
$\mathfrak{C}=\mathcal{F}_{3}^{\,3}\times\mathcal{F}_{4}^{\,5}\times
\mathcal{F}_{5}^{\,4}$ with $\lvert\mathfrak{C}\rvert=17{,}280{,}000$. Read as a
passage:
\[
\text{Category}\to\text{Relation}\to\text{Extension}\to\text{Algebra}\to
\text{Self-reference}\to\text{Closure.}
\]

694	\subsection{Uncertainty and error correction are the composition rule}

870	\section{A worked realization: Optimal Polynomial Intersection}
871	
872	We now turn to a complete worked instance. Here the classical image of a paraconsistent object can be computed directly, and its convergence toward the paraconsistent original can be measured. The object is the tridiagonal ladder of Section 5. The setting is a hard optimization problem whose quantum algorithm is governed by that ladder.
873	
874	\subsection{The problem}
875	
876	\begin{definition}[Optimal Polynomial Intersection]
877	Fix a prime $p$ and an integer $n<p-1$. Let $F_1,\dots,F_{p-1}$ be subsets of $\mathbb{F}_p$. An instance asks for a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[y]$ of degree at most $n-1$ maximizing
878	$f_{\mathrm{OPI}}(Q) = |\{y\in\{1,\dots,p-1\}: Q(y)\in F_y\}|$. It is balanced when every $|F_i|=r=\lfloor p/2\rfloor$.
879	\end{definition}
880	
881	Optimal Polynomial Intersection can be read as a maximum-satisfaction problem over $\mathbb{F}_p$. The bounded-degree polynomials form the codewords of a linear code, so maximizing the intersection count is the same as maximizing the number of constraints satisfied by a codeword.
882	
883	There are $m=p-1$ constraints. Their matrix is Vandermonde, and the dual code $C^{\perp}$ is Reed-Solomon. Berlekamp-Massey performs syndrome decoding of $C^{\perp}$ out to $\ell=\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor$ errors in polynomial time. The problem is a useful hard target because that decoder alone does not reach the optimum. The quantum algorithm improves on the classical baseline by concentrating amplitude on low-weight error patterns.
884	
885	\subsection{The coding structure}
886	
887	The satisfaction problem can be converted directly into a decoding problem. For each constraint $y$, choose a representative of $F_y$ and record a mismatch whenever $Q(y)\notin F_y$. The resulting mismatch vector has one bit per constraint. A polynomial's satisfaction count is therefore $m$ minus the Hamming weight of that vector.
888	
889	The evaluations of all degree-$<n$ polynomials at the $m=p-1$ nonzero points form a Reed-Solomon code $C$ with a Vandermonde encoding. Its dual $C^{\perp}$ is also a Reed-Solomon code, with dimension $m-n$ and minimum distance $d^{\perp}=n+1$. Maximizing satisfaction is thus the same as finding the codeword of $C$ nearest the target in Hamming distance.
890	
891	Berlekamp-Massey decodes the target syndrome with respect to $C^{\perp}$. It forms the syndrome polynomial, finds the shortest linear recurrence that generates it, and reads the mismatch positions from the roots of the error locator. It corrects up to $\ell=\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor = \lfloor d^{\perp}/2\rfloor$ errors in time cubic in the block length. This is the classical polynomial-time floor used here.
892	
893	The same decoding radius $\ell$ bounds the dimension of the ladder matrix. The quantum state is supported on error patterns of weight at most $\ell$, with one weight sector per rung. The condition $2\ell+1<d^{\perp}$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:jordan} is exactly the unique-decodability condition. In that regime, each syndrome names one error pattern, and the ladder transfers amplitude only between adjacent weights.
894	
895	\subsection{The algorithm and its matrix}
896	
897	Decoded Quantum Interferometry~\cite{dqi} prepares a state whose amplitude is concentrated on low-weight error patterns and reads the decoded polynomial. Its expected performance is the largest eigenvalue of a finite matrix.
898	
899	\begin{lemma}[The expected satisfied count]\label{lem:jordan}
900	Let $\langle s^{(m,\ell)}\rangle$ be the expected number of satisfied constraints after state preparation at decoding radius $\ell$. If $2\ell+1<d^{\perp}$, the minimum distance of $C^{\perp}$, then
901	\[
902	\langle s^{(m,\ell)}\rangle = \frac{mr}{p} + \frac{\sqrt{r(p-r)}}{p}\,
903	\lambda_{\max}\bigl(A^{(m,\ell,d)}\bigr),
904	\]
905	with $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ the $(\ell+1)\times(\ell+1)$ real symmetric tridiagonal matrix, diagonal $kd$ for $k=0,\dots,\ell$, off-diagonal $a_{k+1}=\sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$, and $d=(p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$.
906	\end{lemma}
907	
908	This is the result of Jordan and colleagues~\cite{dqi}. Its matrix is exactly the filtration ladder from Theorem~\ref{thm:matrix}. The diagonal term $kd$ is the evaluate operator $D$, with $d=(p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$. The off-diagonal term $\sqrt{(k+1)(m-k)}$ is the raising and lowering coefficient from Theorem~\ref{thm:ladder}. The expected satisfied count is therefore a constant plus the largest eigenvalue of the ladder, multiplied by the stated scale factor.
909	
910	\begin{proposition}[The asymptotic limit]\label{prop:asymp}
911	Taking $\ell\to n/2$ and $m\to p$ gives
912	\[
913	\frac{\langle s\rangle_{\mathrm{DQI}}}{p} = \frac12 + \sqrt{\frac{n}{2p}\Bigl(1-\frac{n}{2p}\Bigr)},
914	\]
915	with no eigenvalue problem to solve.
916	\end{proposition}
917	
918	The finite expression retains the full $(\ell+1)$-dimensional operator. It contains a specific finite $m$, a matrix, and an eigenvector. The asymptotic expression is what remains after that structure is smoothed into a single scalar as $m\to p$.
919	
920	At every finite $m$, the finite form therefore carries strictly more structure than the scalar limit. Moving from the finite operator to the asymptotic scalar is a coarsening, in the same direction as the coreflector of Theorem~\ref{thm:two}.

922	\subsection{The paraconsistent original}
923	
924	We claim the matrix $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is the classical image of a paraconsistent object, and the algorithm's expectation value is that object read through the coreflector. We exhibit the object, the lift, and the identification.

926	The syndrome-decoding structure of the algorithm can be represented as a closing program over the Belnap slice. Its relevant structural feature is an outer frame that banks a count across an uncomputation step.
927	
928	An automatically designed thirty-three-operation program for this structure did not close. The closure audit located the failure precisely. A count was being cleared before the frame that should have banked it had opened. In the language of Lemma~\ref{lem:bank}, the result was exposed instead of banked. The same diagnosis appeared at every rotation of the program's orbit and at the same structural location: reversal cleared the count before its holding frame existed.
929	
930	The composition rule also supplies the repair. Open the holding frame before the computing frame. Implementing that change adds five operations, three splits and two fuses, producing a thirty-eight-operation program that closes. Its banked count survives every reversal. The cyclic verdict closes at every rotation of the orbit, and an exhaustive audit finds the repaired program holding the value at every cut where the original program exposed it.

934	\begin{proposition}[The $m$-fold lift]\label{prop:lift}
935	Let $\iota$ and the coreflector $c$ act coordinatewise on $\{N,T,F,B\}^m$, ordered coordinatewise in the truth order. Then the coordinatewise inclusion is left adjoint to the coordinatewise coreflector, and the Boolean image $\mathbf{B}^m\cong\{F,T\}^m$ is the algorithm's classical register $\mathbb{F}_2^m$.
936	\end{proposition}

938	\begin{proof}
939	For $u\in\mathbf{B}^m$ and $v\in\{N,T,F,B\}^m$, the coordinatewise order gives $\iota^m(u)\leqt v$ iff $\iota(u_i)\leqt v_i$ for all $i$, and $u\leqt c^m(v)$ iff $u_i\leqt c(v_i)$ for all $i$; by Theorem~\ref{thm:two} each coordinate satisfies $\iota(u_i)\leqt v_i \iff u_i\leqt c(v_i)$, so the two coincide. 940	\end{proof}

942	\begin{theorem}[The matrix is the coreflector image of the paraconsistent ladder]\label{thm:main}

954	Both columns of the convergence table below come from one computation, not two sources. Three procedures run every row.

959	\item set $v$ to a random unit vector of length $\ell+1$;

961	\item return $\lambda_{\max}(A) = v^{\top}(A+\sigma I)v - \sigma$.

1028	\section{The arrow of time and the cost of measurement}
1029	
1030	The reversibility of the split and fuse has a thermodynamic reading. Landauer's principle sets a floor on the energy any logically irreversible step must dissipate: erasing one bit of information costs at least $k_B T\ln 2$, because erasure maps two states to one and the lost distinction leaves as heat. Bennett showed that a computation built entirely from reversible steps owes no such cost, since nothing is erased, and Fredkin and Toffoli gave a universal reversible logic that carries this out in principle at no dissipation floor.
1031	
1032	Measurement as filtration is reversible. The split opens a value into tensor factors, a reading selects one, and the fuse restores the whole, so no factor is erased and the ambient pays no Landauer cost for a measurement. What a collapse account records as the destruction of the unread outcomes is, in the ladder, the classical image keeping one rung and dropping the others, and it is only that image, the coreflector's reading, where an erasure and its cost appear. The dissipation of a real measuring device is the cost of maintaining the classical record, not of the filtration itself.
1033	
1034	The arrow of time is the accumulation of fixes. The one operation with no adjoint is the commit, and every commit records a value irreversibly into the winding, a step the fuse cannot undo. A computation of only splits and fuses runs equally well in either direction; a computation that fixes has a direction, the direction in which the fixes accumulate. The thermodynamic arrow, the growth of the classical record, is the count of commits, and the reversibility of the rest is why the ambient itself carries no arrow while its classical image does.
1035	
1036	Approaching the Landauer floor in practice requires the whole computational stack to be aligned. The computation itself must be reversible, with its operations closing so that every step is invertible and its result recoverable. The operating system must also stop erasing, reclaiming transient state by scope teardown rather than abandoning it. The hardware must then implement reversible gates instead of the dissipative gates used by ordinary processors.
1037	
1038	When all three levels are in syzygy, the Landauer floor is approached. If any one level erases, the floor is not reached, and the remaining gap is the erasure forced by that stage. A reversible computation run on an ordinary irreversible stack therefore shows a positive marginal draw above idle. In this account, that draw is the tax of the erasing stack rather than a cost owed by the reversible computation itself.

# Review of UQMds.tex and INDUCTIONn.tex

## UQMds.tex — "Upending Quantum Mechanics"

**1. Central claim.** Quantum mechanics is presented as the classical (Boolean) image of a paraconsistent four/sixteen-valued logic, reached by a lossy retraction; the paper builds "tensor filtration" (raising/lowering/diagonal ladder operators on a many-coordinate register) as the mechanism of measurement, and shows that the tridiagonal matrix governing the Decoded Quantum Interferometry algorithm for Optimal Polynomial Intersection is exactly this ladder read through the retraction, with convergence measured across four problem sizes.

**2. Structural completeness.** Abstract present and states the central distinction (paraconsistent ambient vs. classical restriction) before any notation. Numbered/boxed theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, and definition environments are used throughout (`\newtheorem` chain, shared counter). Proofs are in prose with displayed steps for most results. It ends with an explicit "Discussion" section carrying a clear position/status statement ("Look around you... What occurs is the ambient... The logic is prior to the physics."). It has its own 12-entry bibliography of primary literature (Belnap/Dunn lineage via Shramko–Dunn–Takenaka, Bell, CHSH, Tsirelson, Gleason, Busch, Landauer, Bennett, Fredkin–Toffoli, Golub–Van Loan, plus the DQI paper) at the end. One citation, `golub`, is defined in the bibliography but never invoked with `\cite{golub}` anywhere in the text — a loose end (Section 7.5 describes power iteration, the natural place it would belong).

Minor inconsistency in the proof apparatus itself: some Propositions carry a formal `\begin{proof}...\end{proof}` (e.g. `prop:orders`, `prop:neg`, `prop:diag`, `prop:noinfo`), while others fold the justification into the statement and have no separate proof block at all (`prop:corr`, `prop:context`, `prop:tenths`, `prop:sphere`, `prop:tower`). This is a real stylistic inconsistency against the paper's own declared theorem/proof discipline, not necessarily an error of content.

**3. House-style violations.** One clear violation — narration of a debugging/construction process rather than presented mathematics, in Section 7.4:

> "An automatically designed thirty-three-operation program for this structure did not close. The closure audit located the failure precisely. A count was being cleared before the frame that should have banked it had opened... The composition rule also supplies the repair. Open the holding frame before the computing frame. Implementing that change adds five operations, three splits and two fuses, producing a thirty-eight-operation program that closes."

This is exactly the "what was wrong before / how I fixed it" narration the house style forbids — it describes an automated design attempt, an audit, a diagnosed bug, and a patch, rather than stating and proving a result. No Lean identifiers, branch names, or file paths were found anywhere in the file.

**4. Mathematical gaps.**
- The same Section 7.4 passage above is also a content gap: the "thirty-three-operation program," the "closure audit," and the "thirty-eight-operation program" are asserted as historical fact with no program text, verification trace, or formal statement given in the paper — a conclusion asserted without an argument the reader can check.
- Section 8.4 (uncertainty/error correction): "$\Delta x\,\Delta p \geq c\hbar$... The value of $c$ is determined by the composition rule itself; it is the coefficient that appears when the two exposures are minimized subject to the nesting constraint. In the standard units, this coefficient is $1/2$" — the minimization is described but never carried out; $c=1/2$ is simply stated.
- Section 10: "The taxonomy has a fixed twenty-four-cell structure" is asserted with no derivation of why 24, and the "self-inverse condition selects the positive cells" reasoning is sketched rather than proved.
- The self-citation `\bibitem{gateobstruction}` is to the author's own unpublished "manuscript, 6 August 2026" rather than published primary literature — worth flagging even though not a hard rule violation per se.

**5. LaTeX health — the significant finding.** `\leqi`, `\leqt`, and `\leqc` (the information/truth/constructivity order symbols, used 5, 11, and 3 times respectively starting at Definition "The three orders") are **never defined** anywhere in the file — no `\newcommand`, `\def`, or package that would supply them. As written this document will fail to compile with xelatex (undefined control sequence at every one of these ~19 occurrences, starting at line 183). This is the single most important actionable defect found. Separately, all `\label`/`\ref` pairs resolve correctly and all `\cite` keys have matching `\bibitem`s, and brace/environment counts are balanced (1001/1001 braces; every `\begin{...}` has a matching `\end{...}`), so aside from the missing macro definitions the document is otherwise structurally sound.

**6. Notation inconsistency.** None found beyond the missing-macro issue above; usage of $T,F,t,f,N,B$, the ladder operators, and the coreflectors $c,r$ is consistent from definition through use.

---

## INDUCTIONn.tex — "As Above, Condensed"

**1. Central claim.** Starting from an abstract category and three types of categorical "operations" (logical, inductive, algebraic), the paper claims to derive exactly twelve "primitive" invariants of the "Universal Imscribing Grammar" through a four-stage procedure (alchemically named Separatio/Purificatio/Albedo/Rubedo), closing into a "crystal" of $3^3\times4^5\times5^4=17{,}280{,}000$ types, with a final self-referential closure identity $\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_A$.

**2. Structural completeness.** Abstract is present but drops in unexplained notation early — it states "$\mu\circ\delta=\mathrm{id}_{A}$" in the abstract itself, while $\mu$ and $\delta$ are not defined until the very last section ("The closure"), so the central distinction is not really established before notation. `amsthm` is loaded in the preamble but **no theorem, lemma, proposition, or definition environment is ever used** in the whole document — every claim (the precondition ordering, each Stage's "operation ⇒ invariant" step, "Why exactly twelve") is stated as unboxed prose, with no formal statement/proof pattern at all. Consequently there are no proofs in the sense of displayed argument steps — most derivation lines are bare assertions (e.g. "Both probe the directionality of morphisms and converge on one invariant" for Stage 1, with no actual construction connecting L1/L2 to a specific invariant). It does end with position-like closing sections ("Termination," "The induction in one line"), though these read more as a schematic recap than an argued status statement. It has **no bibliography at all** — no `\begin{thebibliography}`, no `\cite`, despite invoking named external results (K3, FDE, LP logics; Yoneda embedding; Lawvere self-reference; Frobenius law) without a single citation to the literature that defines them.

**3. House-style violations.** No file paths, branch names, Lean identifiers, module names, or "what was wrong before" narration were found in this file.

**4. Mathematical gaps — this is the more serious file.**
- The whole four-stage "induction" never actually gives a function or construction mapping a categorical property to a specific glyph/value; each step is a named assertion ("$\Longrightarrow$") with no argument, e.g. Stage 3: "$\varepsilon_{A}:A\otimes A^{*}\to I\ (\mathrm{A3}) \Longrightarrow \mFid\ (3)\ \text{[unitality of }\varepsilon\text{]}$" — bracketed one-word gloss, no derivation.
- "K3," "LP," and even "FDE" (used differently from UQMds's careful definition) are invoked as established facts ("that partition is the three-valued K3 logic of the algebraic layer... the five-valued LP logic of the gate layer") with zero definition or argument connecting the specific value-counts to these named logics beyond cardinality-matching.
- Section "The closure": tier gaps are given as bare numbers with no formula or computation shown: "$O_{0}\xrightarrow{1.05}O_{1}\xrightarrow{1.30}O_{2}\xrightarrow{1.00}O_{2}^{\dagger}\xrightarrow{4.38}O_{\infty}$" — $O_0,O_1,O_2,O_2^\dagger,O_\infty$ are never formally defined, and the numbers 1.05/1.30/1.00/4.38 are asserted with no derivation anywhere in the file.
- Section 5: "the full induction system sits at address $6{,}687{,}051$ and the imscribing procedure that assigns addresses sits at $12{,}089{,}822$" — both numbers are simply asserted, with no computation shown for how these particular addresses were obtained.
- "The retrosynthetic peel of the induction system itself has exactly twelve steps" (Section "Why exactly twelve") uses "retrosynthetic peel" as an undefined term and treats its step-count as self-evidently equal to the twelve primitives, which is closer to restating the conclusion than arguing it.

**5. LaTeX health.** Braces are balanced (338/338) and every `\begin{...}`/`\end{...}` pair matches (abstract, align*, array, center, document, itemize×4, tabular). No `\ref`/`\cite`/`\label` are used at all, so there is nothing to dangle. One real compile risk: `\newfontfamily\shaw{Trabajo}[Scale=MatchLowercase]` requires a system font named "Trabajo" (a Shavian-alphabet typeface) to be installed; if it is not present on the machine compiling with xelatex, this will fail at the `\newfontfamily` load, and its single use later (`\sh{𐑹}`, line 332) depends on it. This is a plausible-to-likely compile failure depending on the environment, distinct from — and less certain than — the UQMds `\leqi/\leqt/\leqc` bug.

**6. Notation inconsistency within the file.** A concrete, checkable contradiction: in Section 3 (Stage 2 — Purificatio), the derivation explicitly attributes the primitive $\mGran$ to I1 alone:
> "$\operatorname{colim}D\ (\mathrm{I1}) \;\Longrightarrow\; \mGran\ (3) \quad\text{[scope of }\widehat{\mathcal{C}}\text{, fixed once A1 present]}$"

But the summary table in Section 4 lists $\mGran$'s originating stage as "A1, I4" — neither of which matches the I1 attribution given in the derivation, and I4 is elsewhere attributed only to $\mDim$, not $\mGran$. This is an internal inconsistency between the "derivation" section and the "summary table" that an editing pass should reconcile (either the table or the Stage-2 derivation line is wrong).

Additionally, the "twelve primitives" named in this file ($\mDim,\mTop,\mCoup,\mSym,\mFid,\mKin,\mChi,\mGran,\mComp,\mCrit,\mStoi,\mWind$ — dimensionality, topology, coupling, etc.) are an entirely different "twelve" from the "twelve primitive operations" named in UQMds.tex (begin, close, forward, reverse, compose, self-reference, split, fuse, evaluate true, evaluate false, engage, fix). If these two files are meant to be part of one coherent framework, as the prompt frames it, this is worth flagging to the user even though it may be intentional (two different layers of the same "grammar") — nothing in either file cross-references or reconciles the two "twelves," so a reader of both cannot tell whether they are the same set under different names or genuinely disjoint structures.
